$comment: Every file here must keep being refused by the distribution schema 1 reader.
These pin the *shape* of an author's update source. They are separate from the
manifest fixtures because distribution is a separate contract: a plugin may change
how it is published without changing what it is allowed to do, and vice versa.
`messageContains` is asserted case-insensitively so wording can improve; the fact
of the refusal is what must not drift.

source-over-http.json.why: An update source reached over plain HTTP can be replaced in transit by anyone on the path. The signature would still be checked, but the URL is pinned at install and a downgrade to HTTP is not something an author should be able to ship.

source-with-no-keys.json.why: A source with no key can never have an update verified against it, so accepting one would create a plugin that appears to have updates and can never take one.

source-key-wrong-length.json.why: A malformed key must fail when the file is read, in front of the user at install time, rather than months later when an update fails for a reason nobody can act on.

source-unsupported-algorithm.json.why: Naming an algorithm this build cannot verify must be refused rather than ignored. Silently skipping the key would leave the plugin looking signed while nothing checked it.

source-duplicate-key-id.json.why: The key id selects which key verifies a signature. Two keys sharing one makes that selection ambiguous, and an ambiguous verification step is one nobody can reason about.
